column1: bequeath§She bequeathed the entire library to a village that had no librarian, no shelving, and no room large enough to hold it.§她把整座藏书楼**遗赠**给一个既没有图书管理员、没有书架、也没有大到放得下它的房间的村庄。§be-（使）+ queath（说）→ 立遗嘱说定
berate§The coach berated the referee for ninety seconds, earned a red card, and later admitted the call had been correct.§教练**痛骂**裁判九十秒，吃了红牌，事后承认那次判罚是对的。§be-（加强）+ rate（斥责）
bereavement§Bereavement leave at the company is three days, which the new policy extends only if the person who died was immediate family.§公司的**丧亲**假是三天，新规定只在逝者为直系亲属时才延长。§be-（彻底）+ reave（夺走，同 rob 抢劫）
bias§The sample carried an obvious bias: everyone surveyed owned a telephone, in a year when half the country did not.§这个样本带有明显的**偏差**——所有受访者都有电话，而那一年全国有一半人没有。§
bifurcation§The bifurcation of the river marks the old county line, and the two branches have carried different names since 1612.§这条河的**分叉**处标出了旧郡界，两条支流自 1612 年起就叫不同的名字。§bi-（二）+ furc（叉，同 fork 叉子）
bilk§The contractor bilked eleven households out of their deposits and had left the country before the first complaint was filed.§这个承包商**诈骗**了十一户人家的定金，第一份投诉递上去时他已经出了国。§

biologist§A biologist counted the colony every spring for thirty-one years, and her notebooks are now the only record of its collapse.§一位**生物学家**连续三十一年每个春天清点这个种群，她的笔记本如今是它崩溃的唯一记录。§bio（生命，同 biography 传记）+ log（学问）
bizarre§The explanation was bizarre enough to be true: nobody inventing an alibi would place himself in a launderette at 3 a.m.§这个解释**离奇**到反而可信——编不在场证明的人不会把自己安排在凌晨三点的洗衣房。§
bland§The soup was bland to the point of insult, and the chef defended it as a deliberate act of restraint.§这汤**寡淡**得近乎失礼，厨师却辩称那是刻意的克制。§
blatant§The conflict of interest was so blatant that the committee spent longer explaining why it hadn't noticed than fixing it.§这桩利益冲突**明目张胆**到委员会解释自己为何没发现的时间比整改还长。§
blather§He blathered for forty minutes without once naming a number, and the audience left knowing exactly what they had known before.§他**空谈**了四十分钟，一个数字也没说，听众离场时知道的和进场时一模一样。§
blend§The two teas blend into something neither one tastes like alone, which is why the shop refuses to sell them separately.§两种茶**混合**成一种谁单喝都不像的味道，所以店里拒绝分开卖。§
boisterous§The crowd grew boisterous after the second goal, and the stewards abandoned any pretence of keeping the aisles clear.§第二个进球后人群变得**喧闹狂欢**，安保索性不再假装维持通道畅通。§
bolster§Two extra witnesses bolstered a case that had rested, until then, entirely on one photograph of uncertain date.§两名额外证人**加固**了一桩此前完全依赖一张日期不明照片的案子。§
bombast§Strip away the bombast and the manifesto says one thing: the author would like more money for his department.§剥掉那些**大话**，这份宣言只说了一件事——作者想给自己部门多要点钱。§bombast（棉絮填料）→ 塞得鼓鼓的空话
bombastic§The bombastic introduction promised a revolution in physics and delivered a modest improvement in battery life.§这段**夸夸其谈**的引言许诺一场物理学革命，交出的是电池续航的小幅改善。§
boomerang§The accusation boomeranged: within a week reporters had found the same practice in the accuser's own accounts.§这项指控像**回旋镖**一样反弹回来——一周内记者就在指控者自己的账目里发现了同样的做法。§
boon§Cheap night electricity was a boon to the bakery, which now does all its heavy mixing between midnight and five.§廉价的夜间电力是这家面包房的**恩惠**，它如今把所有重活都放在午夜到清晨五点之间。§
boost§A single mention on the evening news boosted applications by four hundred percent, and the office was unprepared for any of it.§晚间新闻的一次提及把申请量**推高**了四倍，而办公室对此毫无准备。§
botch§They botched the restoration so thoroughly that the fresco now has to be described in the catalogue as "after" the original.§他们把修复**搞砸**得如此彻底，这幅壁画如今在图录里只能标注为「仿原作」。§
bountiful§The harvest was bountiful for the third year running, and the price farmers received fell for the third year running too.§收成连续第三年**丰足**，而农民拿到的价格也连续第三年下跌。§bount（好，同 bonus 奖金）
bourgeois§The novel mocks bourgeois anxiety about furniture, then spends nine pages describing a sideboard in loving detail.§这部小说嘲笑**中产阶级**对家具的焦虑，接着又用九页深情描写一只餐边柜。§
brag§He never brags about the record, and most of the people he trains have no idea he once held it.§他从不**吹嘘**那项纪录，他带的人多半不知道他曾保持过它。§
brandish§The man brandished a wrench at the meter reader, and the utility suspended service to the street for two days.§那人朝抄表员**挥舞**扳手，供电公司为此停了这条街两天的服务。§brand（剑／烙铁）→ 举着挥
bravado§His bravado lasted until the first question, at which point he asked whether the session could be rescheduled.§他的**虚张声势**撑到第一个问题为止，那时他就问会不会能改期。§
brevity§The brevity of the reply was itself the message: four words, no greeting, and no offer to discuss it further.§回复之**简短**本身就是信息——四个词，没有称呼，也没有再谈的意思。§brev（短，同 abbreviate 缩写）
bromide§His speech was a string of bromides about hard work, delivered to people who had been laid off that morning.§他的讲话是一串关于勤奋的**陈词滥调**，讲给那天早上刚被裁掉的人听。§溴化物曾用作镇静剂 → 令人昏昏欲睡的老套话
brutality§The brutality of the crackdown was documented by three foreign crews, and the footage circulated before any denial could.§镇压的**残暴**被三家外国摄制组记录下来，画面在任何否认之前就传开了。§brut（沉重／野蛮，同 brute 野兽）
bucolic§The painting is deliberately bucolic: sheep, a stream, and not one hint of the mill that fed the entire valley.§这幅画刻意呈现**田园牧歌**风——绵羊、溪流，看不到一点养活整条河谷的工厂的影子。§bou（牛）+ kolos（牧人）
buffer§A savings account of three months' pay is a buffer, and the households without one absorbed the whole shock at once.§三个月工资的存款是一道**缓冲**，没有这道缓冲的家庭一次性承受了全部冲击。§
bully§He bullied junior staff for years, and every complaint stopped at the same manager who had also been his mentor.§他**霸凌**下属多年，每一份投诉都止步于同一位经理——那位也曾是他的导师。§
bungle§The department bungled the rollout twice, and by the third attempt half the schools had built their own system.§这个部门把推广**搞砸**了两次，等到第三次尝试时，一半学校已经自建了系统。§
buoy§What buoyed the crew through the last week was not hope but routine: three meals, four watches, and no discussion of it.§最后一周**支撑**着船员的不是希望而是常规——三顿饭、四班岗，绝口不谈这件事。§
buoyancy§The buoyancy of the market lasted eleven months, and every forecast issued during it assumed it would last eleven years.§市场的**上扬势头**持续了十一个月，而其间发布的每一份预测都假定它会持续十一年。§
burgeon§The neighborhood's cafés burgeoned from two to nineteen in four years, and the rent went up faster than any of them.§这个街区的咖啡馆四年间从两家**猛增**到十九家，而房租涨得比它们中的任何一家都快。§
buttress§Three independent studies buttress the claim, though all three drew their data from the same municipal registry.§三项独立研究**支撑**着这一论断，尽管三者的数据都取自同一份市政登记册。§ 建筑上的「扶壁」→ 从旁顶住
bypass§Drivers bypass the town entirely now, and the shops that lived on passing traffic closed within two years of the new road.§司机如今完全**绕开**这个镇子，靠过路客生意的店铺在新路通车两年内都关了门。§
cacophonous§The orchestra's warm-up is cacophonous by design: forty players tuning at once, each ignoring everyone else.§乐团的热身**杂乱刺耳**是有意为之——四十名乐手同时调音，各不理会。§caco（坏）+ phon（声音，同 telephone 电话）
cacophony§A cacophony of alarms filled the ward, and after two weeks the nurses no longer heard any of them.§病房里充斥着警报的**刺耳嘈杂**，两周后护士们再也听不见其中任何一声。§
cadent§The prose is oddly cadent, closer to a psalm than to a report, which is exactly why it was so widely quoted.§这段文字奇异地**富有节奏**，更像圣咏而非报告，这正是它被广为引用的原因。§cad（落下，同 cadence 抑扬顿挫）
cajole§She cajoled the landlord into one more month, mostly by remembering the names of all four of his grandchildren.§她**软磨硬泡**让房东又宽限一个月，靠的主要是记住了他四个孙辈的名字。§
callous§The reply was callous rather than cruel: a form letter, correctly spelled, sent to a family that had lost a child.§这封回复**麻木**多过残忍——一封拼写无误的格式信，寄给一个刚失去孩子的家庭。§call（硬皮，同 callus 老茧）→ 心上结了茧
callow§He was callow at twenty-two and knew it, which is the only reason the older engineers were willing to teach him.§他二十二岁时**稚嫩**，而且自己清楚，这是那些老工程师肯教他的唯一原因。§
calumny§The calumny spread faster than the correction, and ten years later people still repeat a charge that was withdrawn in a week.§这桩**诽谤**传得比更正快，十年后人们仍在重复一项一周内就撤回的指控。§calumn（诬告）
camouflage§The building's camouflage is social rather than visual: it looks so ordinary that nobody wonders what happens inside.§这栋建筑的**伪装**是社会性的而非视觉的——它普通到没人好奇里面在做什么。§
candid§Her candid assessment cost her the account and earned her three referrals from people who had watched her give it.§她**坦率的**评估让她丢了这个客户，却从旁观者那里换来三个推荐。§cand（发光／洁白，同 candle 蜡烛）→ 亮堂堂不遮掩
cannibalistic§The practice is cannibalistic in a corporate sense: each new product ate the sales of the one launched a year earlier.§这种做法在企业意义上是**自食其肉**的——每款新品都吃掉一年前上市那款的销量。§
cantankerous§The cantankerous old editor rejected four future prize-winners and was right about roughly half the others.§这位**乖戾易怒**的老编辑退掉了四位后来的获奖者，而在其余稿件上大约对了一半。§
capitulate§The garrison capitulated after eleven weeks, having eaten the horses and burned the furniture for warmth.§守军在十一周后**有条件投降**，此前已吃光了马匹，烧尽了家具取暖。§capit（头，同 capital 首都）→ 逐条（章）议降
capricious§Funding here is capricious: a program that ran for a decade can vanish because one committee member changed jobs.§这里的经费**反复无常**——一个运作十年的项目会因一位委员换了工作而消失。§
captious§A captious reviewer will find eleven typos and never say whether the argument holds.§一个**吹毛求疵**的评审会挑出十一处错字，却从不说论证是否成立。§capt（抓，同 capture 捕获）→ 专抓小辫子
captivate§The first thirty seconds captivated an audience that had come only because the other screening was sold out.§开头三十秒就**迷住**了观众，而他们本来只是因为另一场票卖光了才进来的。§capt（抓，同 capture 捕获）→ 把人心抓住
capture§The camera captured the whole sequence, and the eleven seconds it recorded changed how the department is trained.§摄像机**拍下**了整个过程，它录下的十一秒改变了这个部门的训练方式。§capt（抓，同 captive 俘虏）
career§Her career took a shape nobody plans: eight years of failure, one lucky introduction, and then everything at once.§她的**职业生涯**呈现出无人能规划的形状——八年失败、一次幸运的引荐，然后一切同时到来。§
carnivorous§Carnivorous plants grow where the soil offers almost no nitrogen, so they take it from insects instead.§**食肉的**植物长在土壤几乎不含氮的地方，于是转而从昆虫身上取氮。§carn（肉，同 carnival 狂欢节／告别肉食）+ vor（吃，同 devour 吞食）
casual§His casual remark about the deadline was repeated up three levels and returned to him as a formal commitment.§他关于期限的一句**随口**评论被逐级上报三层，回到他手里时已成正式承诺。§
catalyst§The resignation was the catalyst, not the cause: the department had been failing for years and everyone knew it.§那次辞职是**催化剂**而非原因——这个部门衰败多年，人人心知肚明。§cata-（向下）+ lys（分解，同 analysis 分析）

catastrophic§The flood was catastrophic for the archive: nine thousand volumes went under water that took four days to recede.§这场洪水对档案馆是**灾难性的**——九千册书泡在四天才退去的水里。§cata-（向下）+ stroph（转，同 strophe 诗节）→ 急转直下
categorize§Librarians categorize by subject, booksellers by expected buyer, and the same novel ends up in two entirely different rooms.§图书馆员按主题**分类**，书商按预期买家分类，同一本小说最终落在完全不同的两个房间。§
cathartic§Writing the letter was cathartic even though she never sent it, and she kept the envelope for eleven years.§写这封信有**宣泄疗愈**之效，尽管她从未寄出，那个信封她留了十一年。§kathar（净化）
caustic§His caustic review ended a friendship and, three years later, was quoted approvingly by the author himself.§他那篇**刻薄**的评论断送了一段友谊，三年后却被作者本人赞许地引用。§caus（烧，同 cauterize 烧灼）→ 烧灼般刺人
celebrity§Celebrity arrived too early for him: at nineteen he was recognized everywhere and had made nothing he was proud of.§**名气**对他来说来得太早——十九岁走到哪都被认出来，却还没做出一件自己满意的东西。§celebr（众多／著名，同 celebrate 庆祝）
censure§The board censured him formally and then renewed his contract, which told the staff everything about how seriously it meant it.§董事会正式**谴责**了他，随后续了他的合同，这让员工明白这份谴责有多认真。§cens（评断，同 census 人口普查）
cerebral§His approach is cerebral to a fault: he can prove the strategy works and cannot get anyone to follow it.§他的路数**过于理性**——他能证明策略行得通，却没法让任何人跟着做。§cerebr（大脑）
certitude§Her certitude unsettled the panel more than doubt would have, since none of them could match the evidence to it.§她的**笃定**比怀疑更让评审组不安，因为没人能把证据与之对上。§cert（确定，同 certain 确定的）
chairperson§The chairperson let the argument run twenty minutes past its usefulness, and the vote afterward was worse for it.§**主席**让争论超出有用限度二十分钟，随后的投票也因此更糟。§
champion§She championed the proposal for six years, through three committees and two governments, until it finally became law.§她为这项提案**奔走支持**了六年，经历三个委员会、两届政府，它才终于成法。§camp（战场，同 campaign 战役）→ 上场为人而战
chaotic§The first hour was chaotic: no one knew who was in charge, and three people gave contradictory instructions at once.§第一个小时**混乱不堪**——没人知道谁在负责，三个人同时给出互相矛盾的指令。§
